components.note: 礻 (spirit, altar) — 礼 relates to ceremony and rites performed before the spirits.
乚 reflects the character's phonetic root, though its exact link to the modern reading lǐ is unclear today.
卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'

example.hanzi: 他们要求客人穿礼服出席晚宴。
example.pinyin: Tāmen yāoqiú kèrén chuān lǐfú chūxí wǎnyàn.
example.english: They required guests to wear formal attire to the dinner.
example.fact: The modern tuxedo traces to an 1886 dinner at Tuxedo Park, New York, where a young socialite's shortened black dinner jacket — modeled on a style popularized by the future King Edward VII — broke from the era's mandatory tailcoat. The abbreviated jacket caught on and became the informal blueprint for men's formal wear ever since.

components.note: 臣 here pictures a large, downcast eye, an old image tied to lying down or resting.
卜 (an altered form of 人, 'person') completes the picture of someone lying in bed, giving 卧 its meaning 'to lie down.'
广 (a building/shelter) — 底 relates to the base or bottom, as of a structure
氐 (dǐ) is an exact match for the sound of 底

example.hanzi: 警方派了一名卧底去调查那个犯罪团伙。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng pàile yī míng wòdǐ qù diàochá nàge fànzuì tuánhuǒ.
example.english: The police sent an undercover agent to investigate that criminal gang.
example.fact: FBI agent Joseph Pistone spent six years undercover inside the Bonanno crime family under the alias 'Donnie Brasco,' gathering evidence that led to more than 100 convictions. It remains one of the longest sustained undercover infiltrations in U.S. law-enforcement history.

meanings: special collection of printed or broadcast material

components.note: 专 is the simplified form of 專, which depicted a hand 寸 turning a spindle 叀 to spin thread. The single, focused motion gave 专 its meaning 'specialized, concentrated, exclusive.'
车 (cart) — 辑 originally referred to fitting a cart's parts together, extending to 'gather, compile, edit.'
咠 (qì) is distantly related in sound to jí, sharing the same historical initial series (j/q/x) though the two have drifted apart.

example.hanzi: 这位歌手的新专辑上市后立刻登上排行榜冠军。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi gēshǒu de xīn zhuānjí shàngshì hòu lìkè dēngshàng páihángbǎng guànjūn.
example.english: This singer's new album shot to the top of the charts as soon as it was released.
example.fact: Michael Jackson's 1982 album Thriller remains the best-selling album of all time worldwide, with estimated sales exceeding 70 million copies. It was also the first album to send seven of its nine tracks into the U.S. Top 10 singles chart.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
子 (child/seed) — 存's meaning 'to exist, survive' has been linked to a seed persisting to grow.
才 (cái) gives a sound hint — 存 is pronounced cún, sharing the initial consonant though the vowel and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 请记得随时保存你的工作文件，以免数据丢失。
example.pinyin: Qǐng jìde suíshí bǎocún nǐ de gōngzuò wénjiàn, yǐmiǎn shùjù diūshī.
example.english: Please remember to save your work files regularly so you don't lose any data.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, built into a mountainside on a Norwegian Arctic island, preserves over a million seed samples at -18°C as a backup against the loss of crop diversity. Its remote, cold, geologically stable location was chosen specifically so the seeds could survive power failures, war, or climate disasters.

components.note: 彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 两国领导人会面，试图修好长期紧张的关系。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén huìmiàn, shìtú xiūhǎo chángqí jǐnzhāng de guānxì.
example.english: The leaders of the two countries met, trying to mend their long-strained relationship.
example.fact: In 1972, U.S. President Richard Nixon's visit to China ended more than two decades of diplomatic isolation between the two nations. The trip was so unexpected at the time that it gave rise to the phrase 'a Nixon goes to China,' now used to describe any leader making a surprising political reversal.

components.note: 咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.

example.hanzi: 她的故事深深地感动了在场的每一个人。
example.pinyin: Tā de gùshì shēnshēn de gǎndòngle zàichǎng de měi yī gèrén.
example.english: Her story deeply moved everyone present.
example.fact: Emotional tears carry a different chemical makeup than tears triggered by irritants like onions — they contain stress hormones and natural painkillers called leucine-enkephalins. That difference is part of why crying from strong emotion can leave people feeling physically calmer afterward.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 继 relates to continuing a thread without a break
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 继's reading jì, reflecting sound change over a long time
承 depicts multiple hands supporting and lifting something from below — giving 承 its meaning 'to support, to receive, to inherit.'

example.hanzi: 他继承了父亲的公司和全部财产。
example.pinyin: Tā jìchéngle fùqīn de gōngsī hé quánbù cáichǎn.
example.english: He inherited his father's company and all his assets.
example.fact: Mitochondrial DNA is passed down almost exclusively through the maternal line, since sperm mitochondria are typically destroyed after fertilization. That property lets scientists trace maternal ancestry back tens of thousands of years through a method called mitochondrial DNA analysis.

components.note: 女 (woman) — depicts a wife in the traditional image behind this character.
口 (mouth/words) — the wife following her husband's spoken words gave 如 its meaning of 'as, like, if.'
亼 — traditionally linked to an image of gathering or covering; its original pictorial sense has become obscure, but the character came to mean 'now, the present.'

example.hanzi: 如今很多人都习惯用手机支付。
example.pinyin: Rújīn hěn duō rén dōu xíguàn yòng shǒujī zhīfù.
example.english: Nowadays, many people are used to paying with their phones.
example.fact: China's mobile payment volume surpassed $50 trillion in transactions annually by the early 2020s, driven largely by QR-code systems like Alipay and WeChat Pay that let even street vendors accept payments without ever installing a card reader.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 孩子们放学后喜欢在公园打球。
example.pinyin: Háizimen fàngxué hòu xǐhuan zài gōngyuán dǎqiú.
example.english: The kids like playing ball in the park after school.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in December 1891 by Canadian physical education instructor James Naismith, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony in Springfield, Massachusetts, to give restless students an indoor game to play during the winter.

components.note: 礻 (spirit/altar) — ancestor worship at a family altar ties 祖 to the spirit radical.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to zǔ, having drifted apart over time.
母 depicts a kneeling woman with two dots marking breasts — an image emphasizing nursing and motherhood, giving 母 its meaning 'mother.'

example.hanzi: 我祖母今年八十岁了，身体还很健康。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǔmǔ jīnnián bāshí suì le, shēntǐ hái hěn jiànkāng.
example.english: My grandmother is eighty years old this year and still in good health.
example.fact: The verified oldest person in recorded history, Jeanne Calment of France, lived to 122 years and 164 days, outliving her own daughter and grandchildren. She reportedly took up fencing at 85 and still rode a bicycle at 100.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
父 (father) — 爹 names a family relation, one's father.
多 (duō) gives a sound moderately close to diē, sharing the initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 村里的孩子们都亲切地叫他老爹。
example.pinyin: Cūn lǐ de háizimen dōu qīnqiè de jiào tā lǎodiē.
example.english: The children in the village all affectionately call him 'old man.'
example.fact: In many rural Chinese dialects, kinship terms like 'lǎodiē' extend beyond blood relatives to any respected elder man in the community, reflecting a broader East Asian custom of using family titles as a mark of social respect rather than a literal relation.

components.note: 人 (a man) — the figure straining upward.
止 (feet) — standing up on his feet, or toes, to look into the distance, the image of anticipation giving 企 its meaning 'to look forward to, hope for' and, by extension, 'enterprise' (企业).
图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'

example.hanzi: 警方挫败了那名罪犯企图逃跑的计划。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng cuòbàile nà míng zuìfàn qǐtú táopǎo de jìhuà.
example.english: The police foiled the criminal's attempt to escape.
example.fact: Alcatraz, the maximum-security island prison in San Francisco Bay, recorded 14 separate escape attempts involving 36 inmates during its 29 years of operation. Officially none succeeded, though the fate of three men who vanished during a 1962 attempt has never been conclusively determined.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
女 (woman) — depicts a wife in the traditional image behind this character.
口 (mouth/words) — the wife following her husband's spoken words gave 如 its meaning of 'as, like, if.'

example.hanzi: 与其抱怨，不如想办法解决问题。
example.pinyin: Yǔqí bàoyuàn, bùrú xiǎng bànfǎ jiějué wèntí.
example.english: Rather than complain, it would be better to find a way to solve the problem.
example.fact: Psychologist Barry Schwartz's research on the 'paradox of choice' found that people offered fewer options often report greater satisfaction with their final decision than those given many alternatives, because excess choice increases regret and the sense that a better option was missed.

components.note: Bird — an older semantic root kept from an earlier character shape.
Gives the sound hù, related to gù but drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) sits on the left.
用 (to use) — paired with person 亻, this pictures someone being 'used,' i.e. employed, giving 佣 its meaning 'servant, commission (paid for a service).'

example.hanzi: 这家公司雇佣了两百多名员工。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī gùyōngle liǎng bǎi duō míng yuángōng.
example.english: This company employs more than two hundred staff.
example.fact: The eight-hour workday, now standard across much of the world, grew out of the 19th-century labor slogan 'eight hours for work, eight hours for rest, eight hours for what we will,' first widely championed during the 1886 general strikes in the United States that also gave rise to May Day.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
阝 (hill) — 险 originally referred to steep, dangerous terrain
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 险's reading xiǎn, having drifted apart over time
⺮ (bamboo) — 箱 originally described a bamboo case or chest.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 箱.

example.hanzi: 他把重要文件都锁在保险箱里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhòngyào wénjiàn dōu suǒ zài bǎoxiǎnxiāng lǐ.
example.english: He locked all the important documents in the safe.
example.fact: The vault at Fort Knox, the U.S. Bullion Depository, is protected by a door weighing more than 20 tons and set behind granite walls and steel-lined concrete. Despite its legendary reputation, the facility has never actually been robbed.

components.note: 阝 (mound, related to walls) — 隔 describes something separated by a barrier.
鬲 (gé) is an exact match for the sound of 隔.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

example.hanzi: 医院把患有传染病的病人隔离起来。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn bǎ huàn yǒu chuánrǎnbìng de bìngrén gélí qǐlái.
example.english: The hospital isolated patients with the contagious disease.
example.fact: The word quarantine originates from the Venetian practice, starting in the 14th century, of holding ships arriving from plague-affected ports offshore for 'quaranta giorni' — forty days — before allowing passengers and cargo to land.

components.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 他第一次穿西装去参加面试。
example.pinyin: Tā dì yī cì chuān xīzhuāng qù cānjiā miànshì.
example.english: He wore a suit for the first time to go to a job interview.
example.fact: The modern business suit descends from a 17th-century English fashion reform pushed by King Charles II, who in 1666 decreed a simpler coat, waistcoat, and breeches as court dress to distance England from ornate French styles — a look that gradually evolved into today's suit.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 晓 describes the sun coming up, dawn, and by extension, becoming clear.
尧 (yáo) gives a sound close to xiǎo.
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 我早就晓得他会来。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎo jiù xiǎode tā huì lái.
example.english: I already knew he would come.
example.fact: The 'tip-of-the-tongue' phenomenon, where a person is certain they know a word but cannot recall it, has been documented in nearly every language studied. Researchers attribute it to a temporary breakdown in retrieving a word's sound even though its meaning remains fully accessible.

components.note: 辶 (walk/movement) — 迟 describes moving too slowly, arriving 'late.'
尺 (chǐ) gives a sound very close to chí, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.
日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'

example.hanzi: 谎言迟早会被揭穿。
example.pinyin: Huǎngyán chízǎo huì bèi jiēchuān.
example.english: Lies will be exposed sooner or later.
example.fact: Tectonic plates drift at roughly the same speed fingernails grow, just a few centimeters a year. Yet given enough time this slow creep has torn apart supercontinents like Pangaea and, geologists predict, will eventually reassemble today's continents into a new one, sometimes called Pangaea Ultima, in around 250 million years.

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'

台 was originally its own character, thought to picture a mouth 口 speaking to please someone (an old meaning close to 'pleased, agreeable'). It was later borrowed to write the simplified form of 臺, which depicted a raised earthen platform or lookout tower, giving 台 its modern meaning 'platform, stage, station.'

example.hanzi: 这家电台每天播放新闻和音乐节目。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàntái měitiān bòfàng xīnwén hé yīnyuè jiémù.
example.english: This radio station broadcasts news and music programs every day.
example.fact: On October 30, 1938, Orson Welles's radio dramatization of The War of the Worlds, staged as a series of fake news bulletins about a Martian invasion, reportedly caused real alarm among some listeners who tuned in after the introduction explaining it was fiction.

meanings: (idiom) powerless to do anything about it

components.note: 无 is the simplified form of 無, which originally depicted a person 大 dancing while holding ornamented sleeves or tails, a shaman's ritual dance. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the negation 'not have, without,' while the original dance meaning was taken over by a new character, 舞.
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

为 is the simplified form of 為, which depicted a hand 爪 leading an elephant 象 by its trunk, an image of putting an elephant to work. That picture of purposeful action gave 为 its meaning 'to do, to make, to act as.'
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 面对突如其来的自然灾害，人类有时也无能为力。
example.pinyin: Miànduì tūrúqílái de zìrán zāihài, rénlèi yǒushí yě wúnéngwéilì.
example.english: Faced with sudden natural disasters, humans are sometimes powerless to do anything.
example.fact: The 2011 Tōhoku earthquake off Japan's coast was powerful enough to shift the Earth's axis by an estimated 17 centimeters and shorten the length of a day by about 1.8 microseconds — a reminder of how even the largest engineered defenses can be overwhelmed by geophysical forces of that scale.

components.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
氵 (water) — 涯 originally named the edge or shore of a body of water.
厓 (yá) gives the sound — an exact match with 涯.

example.hanzi: 他的职业生涯长达三十多年。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhíyè shēngyá cháng dá sānshí duō nián.
example.english: His career spanned more than thirty years.
example.fact: Jazz singer Tony Bennett performed publicly for more than 70 years, releasing an album, Love for Sale, with Lady Gaga in 2021 at age 95 while already living with Alzheimer's disease — one of the longest continuously active careers in modern popular music.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'
灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 出国旅行之前，请检查你的护照是否过期。
example.pinyin: Chūguó lǚxíng zhīqián, qǐng jiǎnchá nǐ de hùzhào shìfǒu guòqí.
example.english: Before traveling abroad, please check whether your passport has expired.
example.fact: The modern passport format traces to a 1920 League of Nations conference in Paris, which standardized the small booklet design, photograph requirement, and page dimensions still used by most countries today.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.
讠 (speech) — relates to 识's meaning 'to know, recognize,' knowledge conveyed through words.
只 (zhǐ) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shí.

example.hanzi: 阅读是获取知识的重要途径。
example.pinyin: Yuèdú shì huòqǔ zhīshi de zhòngyào tújìng.
example.english: Reading is an important way to gain knowledge.
example.fact: The ancient Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, is estimated to have held several hundred thousand papyrus scrolls and employed scholars tasked with copying and translating every book that passed through the city's port. Its eventual loss is still cited as one of history's greatest blows to accumulated human knowledge.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 明天上午我们要开会讨论新项目。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān shàngwǔ wǒmen yào kāihuì tǎolùn xīn xiàngmù.
example.english: Tomorrow morning we're going to have a meeting to discuss the new project.
example.fact: A widely cited internal study at Amazon found meetings with more than eight attendees became significantly less effective, leading founder Jeff Bezos to popularize the 'two pizza rule': if two pizzas can't feed the group, the meeting has too many people.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out for support.
十 (a branch) — held in the hand, the image of support giving 支 its meaning 'to support, prop up; branch.'
亻 (a person) — someone receiving something
寸 (a hand) — a hand handing something over

example.hanzi: 你可以用信用卡支付账单。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng xìnyòngkǎ zhīfù zhàngdān.
example.english: You can pay the bill with a credit card.
example.fact: The earliest known use of paper money dates to China's Tang and Song dynasties, around the 7th to 11th centuries, when merchants began issuing promissory notes called 'jiaozi' to avoid carrying heavy strings of copper coins over long trade routes.

components.note: 页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
衤 (clothes) shows 袖 is a part of clothing.
由 (yóu) gives a sound distantly related to xiù, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他被大家推选为团队的领袖。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi dàjiā tuīxuǎn wéi tuánduì de lǐngxiù.
example.english: He was elected by everyone as the team's leader.
example.fact: Antarctic explorer Ernest Shackleton is often studied as a model of crisis leadership: after his ship Endurance was crushed by ice in 1915, he led all 28 crew members to survival over nearly two years, including an 800-mile open-boat journey across the Southern Ocean, without losing a single man.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 昨晚有个小偷闯入了邻居家。
example.pinyin: Zuówǎn yǒu gè xiǎotōu chuǎngrù le línjū jiā.
example.english: A thief broke into the neighbor's house last night.
example.fact: The Mona Lisa's fame skyrocketed after it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 by an Italian handyman who believed it should be returned to Italy. The painting was missing for over two years, and the theft generated more publicity than the artwork had received in the preceding four centuries.

components.note: 见 (to see) — the act of looking.
又 (again, or a hand) — looking closely or repeatedly, giving 观 its meaning 'to observe, view.'
手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'

example.hanzi: 全家人一起观看了世界杯决赛。
example.pinyin: Quán jiā rén yīqǐ guānkànle shìjièbēi juésài.
example.english: The whole family watched the World Cup final together.
example.fact: The 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing broadcast is estimated to have been watched live by roughly 600 million people worldwide — about a fifth of the planet's population at the time — making it one of the largest simultaneous shared television events in human history.

components.note: Hand — shows this is a physical action.
Represents fighting or striving for something.
扌 (hand) — 扎 describes a hand at work tying or binding something.
乚 depicts a bent length of string or cord — bound by the hand 扌, it gave 扎 its meaning 'to tie, to bundle.'

example.hanzi: 溺水的人在水中拼命挣扎。
example.pinyin: Nìshuǐ de rén zài shuǐzhōng pīnmìng zhēngzhá.
example.english: The drowning person struggled desperately in the water.
example.fact: Real drowning rarely looks like the dramatic splashing shown in movies. Lifeguards are trained to recognize the 'instinctive drowning response,' in which a person's arms press down involuntarily at their sides and the head tilts back, making genuine drowning often silent and easy for bystanders to miss.

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 这位球员在比赛中打进了两个球。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi qiúyuán zài bǐsài zhōng dǎ jìn le liǎng gè qiú.
example.english: This player scored two goals in the match.
example.fact: Brazilian footballer Pelé is officially credited by the Guinness Book of Records with 1,279 career goals across professional matches, a tally that includes friendlies and exhibition games, though goals scored in fully competitive matches alone number closer to 767.

meanings: inch (unit of length equal to 2.54 cm.)

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) gives a sound hint — 英 is pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
寸 pictures a hand with a small mark near the wrist, showing the point about an inch up where a pulse can be felt — the image behind its meaning 'inch, small.'

example.hanzi: 这台电视的屏幕有五十五英寸。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái diànshì de píngmù yǒu wǔshíwǔ yīngcùn.
example.english: This television has a 55-inch screen.
example.fact: The inch was historically defined in a 1324 English statute as the length of three barleycorns laid end to end. It wasn't standardized to its precise modern value of exactly 2.54 centimeters until an international agreement among English-speaking countries in 1959.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 推 relates to pushing something with the hand
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 推's reading tuī
艹 (grass) shows this is plant-related.
存 (to survive, endure) shows the grass persisting year after year — this image of something enduring and reliable extended to 荐's meaning 'to recommend.'

example.hanzi: 医生推荐我每天多喝水。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tuījiàn wǒ měitiān duō hē shuǐ.
example.english: The doctor recommended that I drink more water every day.
example.fact: Netflix's recommendation engine is estimated to influence over 80% of the content its subscribers watch. The company famously ran a $1 million open competition, the Netflix Prize, from 2006 to 2009 to find an algorithm that could improve its movie-rating predictions by just 10%.

components.note: 马 (horse) sets the scene — an animal being pestered.
蚤 (flea) sits beside it — a flea biting and irritating a horse, giving 骚 its meaning 'to disturb, to harass.'
扌 (hand) — 扰 describes stirring something up by hand, 'to disturb.'
尤 (yóu) is only distantly related in sound to rǎo — the connection has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她报警投诉遭到陌生人骚扰。
example.pinyin: Tā bàojǐng tóusù zāodào mòshēngrén sāorǎo.
example.english: She called the police to report being harassed by a stranger.
example.fact: The term 'sexual harassment' as a legal concept was coined in 1975 by a group of women at Cornell University organizing around a colleague's experience, and it entered U.S. federal case law within a decade, reshaping workplace policy worldwide.

meanings: to take in and care for

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
儿 (child) — 养 relates to raising and nurturing children or animals
羊 (yáng) gives a sound close to 养's reading yǎng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 这对夫妇决定收养一个孤儿。
example.pinyin: Zhè duì fūfù juédìng shōuyǎng yī gè gū'ér.
example.english: This couple decided to adopt an orphan.
example.fact: Cross-species adoption happens in the wild more often than once assumed. Researchers have documented capuchin monkeys raising an orphaned marmoset and lionesses in Kenya nursing orphaned oryx calves, behavior scientists attribute to strong hormonal caregiving instincts overriding typical species boundaries.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'
火 (fire) — flame at the heart of the picture.
暴 (violent, sudden) — a burst of intense fire, together giving 爆 its meaning 'to explode, burst.'

example.hanzi: 拆弹专家小心地引爆了那枚炸弹。
example.pinyin: Chāidàn zhuānjiā xiǎoxīn de yǐnbàole nà méi zhàdàn.
example.english: The bomb disposal expert carefully detonated the bomb.
example.fact: Modern controlled demolition of skyscrapers relies on precisely timed explosive charges, sometimes delayed by mere milliseconds between floors, so that a building collapses almost straight downward into its own footprint rather than toppling outward into surrounding structures.

components.note: 节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'
日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.

example.hanzi: 春节是中国最重要的传统节日。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié shì Zhōngguó zuì zhòngyào de chuántǒng jiérì.
example.english: Spring Festival is China's most important traditional holiday.
example.fact: The Spring Festival travel rush in China, known as chunyun, is considered the largest annual human migration on Earth, with an estimated three billion trips made across roughly 40 days as people travel home for the Lunar New Year.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
Earth/land — represents property or wealth.
Suggests a great amount, linked to being 'worthy' or 'able to bear.'

example.hanzi: 他的失言让在场所有人都感到难堪。
example.pinyin: Tā de shīyán ràng zàichǎng suǒyǒu rén dōu gǎndào nánkān.
example.english: His slip of the tongue made everyone present feel embarrassed.
example.fact: Humans are the only animal known to blush, a reflex Charles Darwin called 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions.' It's triggered by adrenaline widening the blood vessels in the face and is difficult or impossible to suppress voluntarily.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 硬 describes something as hard and firm as stone.
更 (gèng) gives a sound distantly related to yìng, having drifted apart over time.
丿 (a brushstroke mark) — represents writing or a marking on the surface.
巾 (cloth/silk) — early money was silk cloth marked with a value, giving 币 its meaning 'currency.'

example.hanzi: 他把口袋里的硬币都倒在了桌子上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ kǒudài lǐ de yìngbì dōu dào zài le zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: He poured all the coins out of his pocket onto the table.
example.fact: The earliest known coins were minted in the kingdom of Lydia, in present-day Turkey, around 600 BC, made from a naturally occurring gold-silver alloy called electrum and stamped with a lion's head to guarantee their weight and value.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 许 relates to giving permission through words.
午 (wǔ) gives a hint of the sound — 许 is pronounced xǔ, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud

example.hanzi: 没有经过许可，任何人不得进入这个区域。
example.pinyin: Méiyǒu jīngguò xǔkě, rènhé rén bùdé jìnrù zhège qūyù.
example.english: No one may enter this area without permission.
example.fact: The world's oldest known patent system dates to 1474 in the Republic of Venice, which granted inventors a ten-year exclusive right to their creations, an early legal framework that influenced the patent systems most countries still use today.

components.note: 成's ancient form has been traced to a halberd-shaped weapon, related to 戊, marked with an extra stroke recording the completion of a military campaign or task. That sense of a job finished gave 成 its meaning 'to complete, to succeed, to become.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 这部电影只适合成年人观看。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhǐ shìhé chéngniánrén guānkàn.
example.english: This movie is only suitable for adults to watch.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that the human prefrontal cortex, responsible for impulse control and long-term planning, doesn't finish developing until around age 25 — well after most legal definitions of adulthood, which helps explain why risk-taking behavior tends to peak in the late teens and early twenties.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water that is deep.
罙 (deep) — combined with water, giving 深 its meaning 'deep.'
口 (mouth) — 呼 describes an action of the mouth, such as calling out or breathing.
乎 (hū) gives the sound — an exact match with 呼.
口 (mouth) — 吸 describes breathing in through the mouth.
及 (jí) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading xī has diverged.

example.hanzi: 感到紧张的时候，试着深呼吸几次。
example.pinyin: Gǎndào jǐnzhāng de shíhou, shìzhe shēnhūxī jǐ cì.
example.english: When you feel nervous, try taking a few deep breaths.
example.fact: Slow, deep breathing activates the vagus nerve, which signals the parasympathetic nervous system to lower heart rate and blood pressure. This is the physiological basis for why deliberate deep breathing is one of the fastest, most reliable ways to calm the body during acute stress.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — kissing is done with the mouth.
勿 (wù) gives a sound distantly related to wěn, having drifted apart over time.
亼 depicts a lid or cover fitting down over an opening.
口 represents the container's mouth beneath the lid — together giving 合 its meaning 'to close, fit together, unite.'

example.hanzi: 他的指纹与现场发现的完全吻合。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhǐwén yǔ xiànchǎng fāxiàn de wánquán wěnhé.
example.english: His fingerprints completely matched the ones found at the scene.
example.fact: Even identical twins, who share the same DNA, have different fingerprints. Ridge patterns are shaped partly by random pressure and position variations in the womb rather than genetics alone, making fingerprints one of the few truly unique physical identifiers between twins.

meanings: to collect information and report back

components.note: 氵 (water) forms the flowing liquid part of the picture.
匚 (a container shape) receives the water — together showing water gathering into one place, the source of 汇's meaning 'to converge, to gather.'
扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'

example.hanzi: 每周一，各部门经理都要向总裁汇报工作进度。
example.pinyin: Měi zhōuyī, gè bùmén jīnglǐ dōu yào xiàng zǒngcái huìbào gōngzuò jìndù.
example.english: Every Monday, department managers report their work progress to the president.
example.fact: During NASA's Apollo missions, flight controllers in Houston's Mission Control were organized so each specialist reported status only through a strict radio-call hierarchy — a communication discipline credited with helping the Apollo 13 team methodically diagnose and fix a life-threatening oxygen tank explosion in real time.

components.note: 玉 (jade, shown without its dot) represents something valuable.
厶 beneath suggests something slipping away privately, giving 丢 its meaning 'to lose, to throw away.'
⺼ (flesh/body) — 脸 relates to the face, a part of the body
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 脸's reading liǎn

example.hanzi: 他在众人面前摔倒，觉得很丢脸。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhòngrén miànqián shuāidǎo, juéde hěn diūliǎn.
example.english: He fell in front of everyone and felt very embarrassed.
example.fact: Sociologist Erving Goffman's influential 1955 concept of 'face-work' argued that maintaining social dignity in front of others is a near-universal human concern, and cross-cultural studies have since found that fear of public embarrassment measurably affects decision-making in situations as varied as negotiating and public speaking.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 他吃了不新鲜的食物，肚子很难受。
example.pinyin: Tā chī le bù xīnxiān de shíwù, dùzi hěn nánshòu.
example.english: He ate food that wasn't fresh and his stomach feels terrible.
example.fact: Symptoms of food poisoning can appear anywhere from thirty minutes to several weeks after eating contaminated food, depending on the pathogen: Staphylococcus aureus toxins can cause illness within an hour, while Listeria can take up to 70 days to produce symptoms.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
尸 (body) — 屁 relates to a bodily function.
比 (bǐ) gives a sound only distantly related to pì today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他说的都是放屁，别相信他。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de dōu shì fàngpì, bié xiāngxìn tā.
example.english: What he said is nonsense, don't believe him.
example.fact: The average adult produces about half a liter to two liters of intestinal gas per day, mostly from bacteria in the colon fermenting undigested carbohydrates. Beans are a notorious culprit because they contain raffinose, a sugar humans lack the enzyme to break down before it reaches gut bacteria.

components.note: 壴 pictures a drum standing on a base.
支 (zhī) gives a sound distantly related to gǔ, having drifted apart over time; it also pictures a hand holding a drumstick.
手 (hand) — 掌 names the palm, part of the hand.
尚 (shàng) gives a rhyme close to zhǎng, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 演讲结束后，观众们热烈鼓掌。
example.pinyin: Yǎnjiǎng jiéshù hòu, guānzhòngmen rèliè gǔzhǎng.
example.english: After the speech ended, the audience applauded warmly.
example.fact: Researchers studying crowd acoustics have found that applause naturally synchronizes into rhythmic clapping within about 10-20 seconds when an audience wants to signal enthusiasm, then breaks back into random, faster clapping when the goal shifts to simply making the most total noise.

components.note: 方 here depicts a flag or banner, marking a group on the move.
氏 depicts a person following behind — together, a group traveling together, giving 旅 its meaning 'trip, journey.'
禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这次穿越沙漠的旅程非常艰难。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì chuānyuè shāmò de lǚchéng fēicháng jiānnán.
example.english: This journey across the desert was extremely difficult.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway, spanning roughly 9,289 kilometers between Moscow and Vladivostok, is the longest single railway line in the world, crossing eight time zones and taking about a week to travel end to end.

components.note: 大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

example.hanzi: 因为业绩出色，他今年拿到了一笔可观的奖金。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi yèjì chūsè, tā jīnnián nádào le yī bǐ kěguān de jiǎngjīn.
example.english: Because of his outstanding performance, he received a substantial bonus this year.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize's cash award, funded from the estate of dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, has fluctuated with the endowment's investment returns over more than a century. In 2023 the prize amount per category was 11 million Swedish kronor, worth just over $1 million USD, split among winners when a category has multiple laureates.
